ratings_why.fun: Choosing which of their units the enemy hits is a real placement puzzle every turn, and growth runs cleanly from Little Phos through Joan to Ignis; Lost-reading cards feel a bit samey and Spunkie goes dead late.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because its damage is borrowed: a misled enemy carry kills its own board, so the tribe gets stronger as the lobby gets stronger, an axis no current tribe or typical auto-battler tribe has.

verdict_why: Stingy Jack's gold cost is free under uncapped carryover and the Reflection's double damage needs one line of rules; both are small real fixes.

points.text: Unspent gold carries over uncapped, so holding 3 gold costs nothing after the first turn and Stingy Jack is a free permanent Lantern every turn; holding 3 is always right. Tie it to something that costs, such as gold spent this turn.
Black-Water Reflection: say whether double damage applies only to the misled attacker's hit or also to the unit it hits striking back.
Against one tall enemy a misled attack hits nothing and the Lamp Row stalls into ties. Let a misled attack with no other target walk into the bog and hit the attacker itself.
Captain Spunkie's discount is dead text at Tier 6; let it turn into a free refresh per Lost once you can't tier up.

standouts.why: Old Will turns the seed into a rule: their carry hits their other carry. A capstone you build towards.
Sunken Causeway Lights makes leaving gaps a decision, and its Stones feed Foxfire Stump and Tiddy Mun.
Hoard Mere Light turns the enemy's own deaths into your late-game stats, a fresh payoff.

weakest.why: Captain Spunkie never attacks and his only text dies once you reach Tier 6.
Fresh-Ink Mapseller is flat gold on a count, with no choice in it.
Gaffer Turncoat's main line only matters in the mirror; the swap is a one-off.

flags.note: Ignis Fatuus has no cap: with Old Will, the Causeway and Follette, 10 to 15 misleads a fight give every other unit +10 to +15 each permanently each fight, doubled when golden.
Old Will plus Black-Water Reflection and stacked Lanterns can make the enemy's board kill itself before it touches you; few counters exist outside Start of Combat damage.
Near-free permanent Lanterns from Stingy Jack are the main road to the 12-Lantern front-row lock.
Double damage on misled attacks: unclear whether the struck unit's return damage doubles too.
